lines.en: And our segment focusing on Rin Rokuhara begins.
: Yo!
Rin Rokuhara, locally renowned bisexual, had been feeling rather conflicted lately. But I’m less inclined to compare her to an elder beast foraging for berries and more inclined to just compare her.
She wasn’t as [[successfully] outgoing as Chika Chosokabe. Nor did she possess the unabashed kindness demonstrated on a routine basis by her roommate Futaba Fukuyama.
But she did have something that set her apart from both of them.
A cool, skull-shaped hairpin that she bought from a discount store at the mall that she has decorated her many different hairstyles with ever since.
It wasn’t perfect. And she wished there could be something a little more impressive about her when compared to everyone else, but she was fine with being mostly unremarkable.
She was fine with taking the backseat, as evidenced quite literally by her claiming the stereotypical “protagonist’s chair” in the back corner of the classroom on the first day of school.
If she was going to be ordinary, she would be the most spectacular ordinary person she could be.
Only in short bursts, though, as it didn’t take long as the center of attention for her to start crumbling.
And to revisit what I mentioned just moments ago about her currently being conflicted, conflict as a whole was the whole idea conflicting her. Do you follow?
No? Then allow to me put it in plainer terms.
Rin Rokuhara didn’t like what she was currently feeling. And that really pissed her off because it wasn’t every day she got to feel anything at all.
She was bitter, but not too bitter about the break-up. She didn’t mind that the collective mindset of her class was rapidly deteriorating. She just wanted to stop being jealous.
Because if she began to want what everyone else wanted, it would only make things harder. And she was finally in a good spot.
But as she stepped into the cafe, she subconsciously scanned the room for someone she knew would not be there.
And this is why she was feeling conflicted.
Because it meant what she didn’t want it to mean.
: Yeah. Is that okay?
: You know where the keys are, right?
: Sorry to interrupt your call, but I need to-
: Rin, hold on. Sorry, can you say that again?
: No, they’re next to the stove in a wicker basket.
: Wicker. It's that weird...straw stuff. How do you not know what wicker is?
: Just look in the basket. You do remember how to drive, right?
: If you are lying to me right now-
: Yeah. Next Sunday. Got it.
: I’m sending one of my girls to help you right now.
: You’re doing what?
: Can you pick her up here? Or-
: What? Why not?
: Hellooo? Haruka? Your employee of the month would like to clock in now.
: Fine. Whatever. Just...hold on. I have to tell Rin.
: Rin, I need your help with something.
: Is that something...making coffee? Because my skill-set is pretty limited and that’s all I get paid to do.
: No. One of our brewers stopped working and I need you to go with a friend of mine to pick a new one up. And don’t forget to get a receipt or it’s coming out of your paycheck.
: What? Me? Why me? Why can’t your friend just do it if she’s already going?
: Because I don’t trust her to get the right one and you can’t drive yet.
: Hm? Oh, no. You heard that correctly. I said I didn’t trust you.
: Hah...
: Obviously because I don’t trust you. But yeah. I’m sending her now. Just make sure to tell me where you’re picking her up since you refuse to come here for some reason.
: Got it. Thanks. Bye.
: Okay. Sorry. Crazy night. Let me write down the model number and-
: What’s wrong? Why do you look so sad? Shouldn’t you be excited to get out of work? We’re slammed tonight.
: Hell yeah we are, which means it’s the best time to show you what I’m made of. How am I supposed to fight for a promotion if I’m spending my time away from the store? Just have Molly do it.
: Molly called out. Something about a...Pal-world? Do you know what that is? Some kind of convention?
: Oh, that fucking bitch.
: Whatever the case, do this and you can have the promotion. Nobody else is qualified anyway.
: Wait, really?!
: Yeah. I’ll start training you on paperwork later tonight.
: And, just to clarify, this promotion includes a raise, right?
: Obviously. I just have to run some numbers and-
: Wait, we’ll talk about this later. I need you out of here now.
: Got it! I still don’t know where I’m going, though.
: Neither do I. Just pick a direction and...run that way while I follow up with my friend. Worse comes to worst, you have to turn around.
: Choose a direction and run! Got it!
: Wait! Leave your bag here. It’ll weigh you down.
: Roger!
And so Rin Rokuhara takes off in an undisclosed and random direction...
Which, of course, winds up being the wrong direction. And she then has to turn around after two minutes of sprinting.
Twenty minutes go by...and the brisk air of a spring night enters her lungs as she breathes a shallow sigh of relief at the prospect of being able to inhale without burning up from the inside out.
She was glad summer had reached its end. And she was glad that she could take this season as an opportunity to start over.
: Hah...hah...hah...
“But where do I start from?” she wondered, sweat trickling down her chest as the night air fought to cool her down.
“What are my goals? What do I want?”
The promotion was already a lock unless Haruka changed her mind. So Rin needed to come up with something else or face the fact that, for the first time in her life, she’d have nothing to chase after.
Nothing attainable at least. But it wasn’t all that long ago that she wholeheartedly believed finding a girlfriend was a feat so far out of reach that words like “plausible” would make her laugh.
She avoided making eye contact with the stars as she worried it would motivate her to shoot for them.
And as a distant voice approached from beyond the darkness, she decided it would be best to keep these thoughts buried in the back of her head for now.
Just...she worried that she wouldn’t be able to force them back as far as they’d been before.
For they had always been there, but they’d never been this violent. And they’d never been this desperate.
Her eyes scan her surroundings once more, but it’s hopeless.
: Oh! Okay, I see her. I think. Maybe?
: Did she bleach her hair? I don’t remember- actually. Hold on. I’ll just ask.
: Hi! Rin, right?
: Sana’s...mom?
: Yup! The eagle has landed, Haru-chan. I will now be hanging up the telephone.
: And thanks again for letting me borrow your car! A thing I totally did!
: Nope! Sorry! Going through a tunnel! In your car! Bye!
: Whoops. I accidentally hung up.
: Hi! You can call me Sara, not “Sana’s mom.”
: Heeey. And...you can call me Rin. Because...that is my name. My name is Rin.
: It sure is.
: Well, this is awkward.
: I don’t normally hang out with my daughter’s friends. And whenever I do, my daughter is typically...you know...present.
: Y-Yeah...But...we’re not technically hanging out. This is a business thing. We’ve gotta...go...touch a machine. With our hands.
: Yeah, about that.
: No we don’t.
: I’m sorry, what?
: Haru-chan said some guy in a purple hat fixed the machine for her, so we don’t need to go and buy a new one now.
: So...we came all the way here for nothing?
: Hey, at least you ran! I had to take a taxi here and now I’m out like 4,000 yen.
: Taxi? I thought Haruka was letting you borrow her car?
: She was! But she’s also under the impression that I know how to drive when I’ve only been behind the wheel of a car a few times in my life and they’ve all been absolutely terrifying.
: Why didn’t you just tell her that? She would have called us both a taxi if she knew.
: Because now she thinks I’m cooler since I know how to drive.
: But you don’t know how to-
: Shhhh...that will be our little secret.
: Well...does this mean I have to run all the way back to the cafe? Because I don’t have enough money on me to pay for a taxi and I’m not going to make my friend’s mom buy me one.
: But what if I buy myself a taxi over to Koi Cafe and you just happen to...also get inside of it? That would work, right?
: But if we show up in a taxi, Haruka will know that-
: So we have them stop a block away! You need to learn to start thinking outside of the box if you’re ever going to convince people you’re cooler than you actually are, Rin. Take it from me.
: No, I get it. I keep a skateboard in my dorm and I don’t even know how to ollie.
: And I don’t even know what an ollie is so we’re already on the same page!
: We’re the same height too and it’s kind of making me uncomfortable.
: But it’s making me feel young and that’s all that really matters.
: So...I guess we just...go back now? And this whole trip was pointless? And I lose my promotion because Haruka sees it as a loophole and realizes I accomplished nothing tonight?
: Oh, stop. Haru-chan wouldn’t do something like that to you. I’ve heard her talk about you plenty of times before and I can assure you that basically all of it has been good.
: Basically all of it?
: She’s mentioned that you can get a little distracted when cute girls show up but, let’s face it, don’t we all?
: To be completely honest, it’s taking everything I have to even form complete sentences in front of you right now.
: Because I’m young and beautiful, right? Say it. Tell me I’m young and beautiful.
: I’m not sure I can do that without getting a nosebleed.
: Booooooo. This way!
: Wait! Sana’s mom!
: Sara!
: S-Sara! Where are you going?! I thought we were calling a taxi?
: It’ll be faster from the park! Trust me! I’ve been pretending to be cool longer than you’ve been alive!
And so two unlikely girls, forced together by the swift hands of a woman with massive breasts, make their way to a nearby park.
It is a park where strange things have occurred on several occasions before. And, believe it or not, these two bear a special connection to the girl those strange things have revolved around.
As they sit on a bench and wait for a taxi to arrive, the pressure begins to mount. They know they’re supposed to be talking right now. But what are they supposed to talk about?
And why is it so difficult when they have so much in common?
Neither one can ollie. Neither one can drive. Even the fantasies that enshroud their minds when they touch themselves are similar.
It wouldn’t be right to talk about those, though. Not during their first meeting on this bench at least. Something like that would have to wait until the third or fourth or fifth time.
: Do I make you uncomfortable, Rin?
One of them was used to breaking awkward silences like this. But despite how many times she’d done it before, she had never gotten good at it.
: Huh? Not really. Why?
Regardless of that, though, she tried.
: Just wanted to make sure. I’ve been told I can come off a little strong before. And I can imagine it’s already kind of weird to be chatting with your friend’s mom in the first place.
: It’s not that weird. I have like, twice the amount of experience when it comes to talking to moms that most people do. I’d be way more uncomfortable if you were Sana’s dad.
: Well, that’s reassuring to hear. Because I was about your age when I first met him and I was definitely not uncomfortable despite the...admittedly massive age gap.
: He was older than you? By how much?
: A lot. He was my teacher. But I was pretty attention-starved back then, so that didn’t really matter to me.
: Your teacher? Really?
: Mhm. I was a freshman in high school. Just like you now.
: Do you...do you regret it? Looking back on it now?
: Why would I regret it? I got the world’s most adorable little girl out of the deal, so I think it’s pretty safe to say I came out on top. Even if I had to raise her on my own.
: Was it hard?
: Oh god, yeah. I still have no idea how I managed. But Sana turned out perfectly, so I guess I didn’t make too many mistakes.
: Let’s not talk about me, though. My story’s long and confusing, and I want to know more about you. Sana doesn’t really open up much when it comes to her friends.
: Ayane’s really the only one I know anything about. And even that’s mostly surface level stuff.
: I don’t mind opening up. You seem like a good person. I’m just-
: Not sure what you can tell me since it’s the first time we’ve really talked and you don’t fully trust that it’ll stay between us?
: Something...like that.
: I’m sure I’d have said the same thing in your shoes. My experience with adults when I was younger wasn’t exactly great.
: It’s not that I have bad experiences with adults or anything. There’s just...a lot of stuff I know that could mess up basically everything if it gets out.
: And it’s gotten to the point where I have to think like, five times more carefully about every single thing I say so nothing is ruined.
: I’m going to have to start keeping a notebook soon. I can barely remember who knows what at this point. Like, half the class probably doesn’t even know I kissed Sana yet.
: You what?
: See?! Fuck! I didn’t last five seconds! There’s no room in my stupid brain for any more secrets! This is getting too hard!
: You...kissed Sana?
: No.
: That was a lie.
: Why are you lying about lying?
: I have no idea what you’re talking about. Anyway, time to move on.
: Are you two...dating?
: What?! No no no no no! It’s nothing like that! In fact, it’s nothing at all! But if it was anything at all, which it’s not, it would have just been...like...a Christmas party thing.
: Huh.
: Uhh...please don’t mention this to her. I don’t want her to think I...blabbed about anything else.
: I won’t mention anything, don’t worry. I’m just not really sure how I feel about...finding this out from you instead of her.
: I’m not sure what I was expecting, though. It’s not like she ever opens up about anything in the first place.
: I swear, between her and Sensei it’s like I’m constantly trying to pry open a locked diary. So hearing you accidentally confess things like that is a breath of fresh air, weirdly enough.
: You’re...close with Sensei too?
: I like to think so...but I can’t help but question it at times. Especially lately.
: We’ve got that in common, then. It’s kind of embarrassing to say this, but...Sensei’s kind of, like...tied for the role of my best friend.
: Like, he knows things about me that even my roommate doesn’t and I’ve been with her since middle school.
: Does he know you kissed my daughter? Because I can’t fault you for keeping it a secret, but I can sure as heck blame him.
: I’m just going to do that thing where I laugh and avoid the question. Hahaha. Ha.
: You’re funny. I can see why my daughter kissed you.
: Okay, we can stop bringing that up now.
: Do you like her? Be honest.
: Sana? No! It’s...It’s nothing against her. Like, she’s a great friend and an awesome girl. But I don’t think the two of us...
: I don’t really feel that way about her. She was just one of many casualties in this year’s game of spin the bottle.
: Darn. And here I was hoping for a second daughter.
: Sorry to disappoint you. I don’t think either of my moms would be happy if I abandoned them for you, though.
: Hey, you’ve already got two. What’s one more?
: Good point. Plus, it’d be four counting my bio-mom. And five if we want to throw Haruka into the mix as my work mom. How many more do you think I need before setting some kind of record?
: So you’re the...adopted child of two women? I was wondering what you meant by that “double the experience with moms” thing.
: You could’ve just asked, you know. It’s not really a thing I hide. I love my parents.
: Not everyone does, though. And that can be a touchy subject for a lot of people. Especially people you barely know.
: Good point. But even the touchy stuff like my biological parents doesn’t really get to me the way most people expect it to.
: Then, do you mind if I just come out and blatantly ask what could possibly compel a couple to give up someone as cute as you?
: Beats me. My skull was still all soft and weird back then.
: All I know is that my bio-mom was clinically insane and my dad...is a human being who exists. Or existed. He’s the biggest question mark in my life, to be completely honest.
: Probably just another jerk like Sana’s dad — some guy who runs off before he ever has the chance to realize how wonderful his daughter is.
: Probably. No use in turning over any stones to find out, though. Not when I have a trillion other issues that need addressing first.
: Well, hey...
: If your three other good moms are ever busy and you’re in need of a fourth one to accidentally spill more of your secrets to...
: You know where my bar is.
: Only if you’re comfortable with it, though. I get that we might be moving a little quickly right now. I’m just a little weak when it comes to Sana and her friends.
: Especially friends that might turn into more than friends if they keep kissing at Christmas parties.
: Okay. I would like the taxi to arrive now.
: Hahahahaha!
The night is far from over as Rin and Sara wait for their car to arrive.
But that doesn’t stop someone miles away from putting an end to it early.
: I hope tomorrow is better than today.
He collapses into the bed.
He accepts that it won’t be.
Rin and Sara are now friends!
